candidate_decisions.reason: The trusted channel nomination is activated by the pericope's contrast between passing signs while turning aside (12:105), belief mixed with association (12:106), historical travel and inspection (12:109), and stories named as lesson and guidance (12:111). All seven nominated focus branches land; the Fatiha material is handled as a separate overlay.

The supplied coordinates and roots match the thin scent, dismissal as deviation, herald, restored seeing, and knowledge contrast in 12:94-96. The focus return through basira supports the attributed reading while the singular-miracle alternative remains open.

The dream's realization, release from confinement, hidden continuity, and prayer for surrendered completion make the preceding life-story available as an image for sabili. The speaker in 12:108 is not identified as Yusuf, so the retained relation is an analogy between story-shaped trajectory and proclaimed path, not a claim that the focus speaker is recounting his own biography. All nominated branches and both context ayat remain represented.

12:102 explicitly frames the preceding story as unseen news revealed to an absent addressee; the focus then opens with commanded speech. The exact trace roles support a qualified reception-to-public-relay reading without claiming that the focus merely repeats that report.

12:103-104 support the no-wage, reminder, and non-control-of-uptake core: eagerness does not make most people believe, no wage is requested, and the message is remembrance. They do not establish the broader claim that the call is without force, so that implication is not retained; all traced branches and both context ayat remain in the bounded finding.

12:105 names signs, passing over them, and turning aside in one scene; the focus supplies the path and inner insight that make attentive passage a specific contextual reading. Every nominated branch is represented as attributed or by its exact focus facet.

The exact 12:106 surface coordinates belief and association in the same majority subject, and the focus returns through its own first-person refusal of association. This supports an internal-audit reading alongside the external-class reading, not in place of it.

12:107's sudden arrival, enveloping scale, and absent awareness make the following call temporally urgent. The text does not establish that the call trains perception or prevents the event, so the retained core is timely summons before surprise; all traced branches remain as its attributed context.

12:109 supplies human messengers, settlement origins, travel, inspection of outcomes, and reasoning next to the focus's path and followers. This makes an evidence-facing historical dimension of the path available, but 12:109 does not identify its travel imperative's audience as the focus's followers; the finding preserves that distinction and does not make sabili literally mean traveler.

The exact 12:110 sequence runs from the messengers' despair and uncertain attribution of falsehood through aid and rescue, returning to basira and following. It supports insight and fidelity through a crisis while the grammatical alternative about who takes whom to be false remains unresolved.

12:111 explicitly joins tracked stories, lesson, non-fabrication, detail, and guidance. Beside the focus's path, following, and insight, these exact traces support a bounded reading of narrative as a path-making instrument without making it the exclusive source of guidance.

The 12:105 word coordinate carries the supplied root س م و, and that context root cue exposes root_001650/B001 as an available cross-root mark image; the same verse supplies explicit signs and the focus returns through basira. Retain the surprising relation as exploratory and attributed, with no invented gloss or facet and no direct-gloss claim for heavens.

findings.title: A path made attentive by following
findings.claim: The focus's path is a way of responding to signs through discernment, following, and historical inquiry, with its direction clarified by transcendence and refusal of association.
findings.mechanism: In 12:105, people pass signs while turning away; 12:109 then sets human messengers beside travel, inspection of prior outcomes, and reason, while 12:111 names the stories a lesson and guidance. These scenes give the focus's path, call, basira, and followers a specific practice: passage becomes sign-reading, and following becomes a directed response rather than bare assent. The nearby account of mixed belief in 12:106 sharpens the focus's declarations of transcendence and disassociation.
findings.reader_payoff: The followers appear as participants in attentive, evidence-facing movement toward Allah, not merely listeners to a claim.
findings.containment: This is a pericope frame around the focus's ordinary call and path. It does not identify every traveler in 12:109 as a focus follower or replace other live readings of the call.

epistemic.reason: The channel support is a nomination; its specific relation is grounded here in the supplied local focus branches and exact pericope surfaces.

findings.title: The host preface frames the destination in mercy

findings.mechanism: The focus names Allah as the destination of its call, and the automatic host basmala names Allah with two mercy epithets. The repeated divine name connects the later destination to the opening frame, so the call can be read as an approach to the mercifully named One as well as a response to warning.
findings.reader_payoff: The destination of the call is introduced through both invitation and warning; the warning does not exhaust the host's way of naming Allah.
findings.containment: The basmala is a host-prefatory frame, not a promise made by 12:108 about uptake or outcome. It does not undo the warning or make the focus call only a message of comfort.

epistemic.reason: The prefatory and focus surfaces are exact in the packet, while their framing relation is contextual inference and has no separate trust label.

findings.title: Insight carried before consensus
findings.claim: The story allows insight to register a thin sign before social confirmation, endure dismissal, and become legible through later arrival and restored sight.
findings.mechanism: The scent in 12:94 is reported before the family accepts it; 12:95 answers with an accusation of old deviation, and 12:96 brings the herald and restored seeing. The focus's basira can therefore name recognition carried through a hostile interval rather than certainty certified by consensus.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can see how a perception may be real in the story before others have grounds to share it, while later evidence changes what they can recognize.
findings.containment: The restored sight is a singular event in the story; this reading does not make every dismissed intuition true or turn the focus into a guarantee of later validation. The alternative that 12:96 is a unique miracle remains live.

epistemic.reason: All traced context coordinates match the supplied roots and surfaces, but the HFT reader is legacy_unbound and the extension from one story episode to the focus is interpretive.

findings.title: A reminder beyond control of uptake
findings.claim: The focus's call is framed as lucid direction and remembrance rather than a transaction or a response it can compel: most people do not believe even when the messenger is eager, and no wage is requested.
findings.mechanism: 12:103 separates the messenger's desire from most people's belief; 12:104 removes payment and names the message a reminder. These conditions contact the focus's invitation and shift its measure from conversion or compensation to faithful direction and remembrance.
findings.reader_payoff: Low uptake need not read as a failed transaction, and the call's work remains meaningful as reminder.
findings.containment: The evidence supports absence of payment and control over uptake, not a general doctrine that every form of force is absent. It does not settle the audience's response or say that conversion is irrelevant.

epistemic.reason: The supplied context coordinates are exact and mutually reinforcing, while the HFT source is legacy_unbound and the broadest non-coercion implication has been narrowed.

findings.title: Passage that reads its signs
findings.claim: The focus's path and basira can be read as attentive passage through a sign-bearing world: people move across the signs while turning aside, whereas the announced path makes movement responsive to what is encountered.
findings.mechanism: 12:105 places a manifest sign, passing, and bodily turning away in one scene. Contact with the focus's extended path and inner apprehension changes the contrast from moving versus standing still to traversing while reading versus traversing without encounter.
findings.reader_payoff: Insight appears as a manner of moving through the world, not merely a stock of correct information carried along it.

findings.title: Association examined from within belief

findings.mechanism: The focus's final self-disassociation immediately follows the contextual sentence where belief and association coexist. General sharing supplies the admixture image, while the specific association branch returns through the focus's own word for associators.
findings.reader_payoff: The last clause can speak as self-examination as well as a boundary drawn between groups.
findings.containment: The text also permits a straightforward external-class contrast. This finding does not claim that every believer has the same mixture or prescribe a psychological diagnosis.

epistemic.reason: The immediate context and focus surface are exact, while the reflexive application is an attributed inference.

findings.title: A call before sudden arrival
findings.claim: The warning of an enveloping event that arrives suddenly to people unaware gives the following call on insight a temporal urgency: it is an address made while response is still possible.
findings.mechanism: 12:107 pairs encompassing arrival with suddenness and lack of awareness. The focus answers with a call grounded in basira, so the call can be received against the possibility of discovering the horizon only after it arrives.
findings.reader_payoff: The invitation reads as timely address, not only as an abstract statement with no relation to when it is heard.
findings.containment: The sequence does not prove that the call prevents the event or trains a particular faculty. The reading preserves 12:107's warning and the general content of the focus.

epistemic.reason: The traced forms and coordinates match, while the temporal relation from warning to call remains an attributed inference.

findings.title: Following within historical inquiry

Their contact makes the path more than assent alone, while keeping the travelers' grammatical audience distinct from the focus's followers.
findings.reader_payoff: Following can be perceived within a historical practice of observing what happened and drawing reasoned guidance from it.
findings.containment: The imperative in 12:109 may address skeptics rather than define the followers in 12:108. The traveler branch is an attributed metonymic image around the focus's path, not a direct gloss of sabili as a person.

findings.title: Insight through an evidential crisis
findings.claim: 12:110 lets insight and following include an interval in which hope has ended and the messengers' reception of the message is unstable, before aid and rescue arrive.
findings.mechanism: The focus's basira and following meet a sequence of despair, uncertain expectation, an unresolved attribution of falsehood, aid, and separation into safety. This changes insight from an assumed state of continuous emotional certainty into a path that can remain held through an evidential crisis.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can recognize fidelity in a difficult interval without being told that the interval is itself proof of error or proof of vindication.
findings.containment: The compact wording in 12:110 leaves live alternatives about who takes whom to be false. This finding does not decide that syntax, call doubt the correct reading, or guarantee immediate aid.

epistemic.reason: The exact trace coordinates match the supplied verse and focus; the account of insight through crisis is an attributed contextual inference with an unresolved syntactic alternative.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Insightful following may persist through a period when hope has collapsed.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss is supplied; no general statement about all despair is made.

findings.title: Story as a path-making instrument

findings.mechanism: Tracked story and lesson in 12:111 meet the focus's branches of following and inner discernment. Non-fabrication, detailed exposition, and guidance give that tracing an evidential and directional result, so narrative does not merely illustrate the path but can enact how a reader crosses from events to insight.
findings.reader_payoff: The story's sequence becomes a way of learning rather than a container that could be replaced by a list of principles without loss.
findings.containment: 12:111 does not name the focus's path or state that narrative is the only means of guidance. It supplies one local enactment of the path while the focus's ordinary invitation remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The trace coordinates match and the closing verse supplies lesson, detail, and guidance, but identifying its story form as the focus's path remains an attributed interpretation.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Narrative traces can carry a reader toward insight.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss is supplied; this does not exhaust the meaning of the story.

findings.title: Heavens as an exploratory marked surface
findings.claim: Exploratorily, 12:105's heavens can be pictured as a marked surface, and the focus's basira as the capacity to read impressions that ordinary passage leaves unnoticed.
findings.mechanism: The focus's inner discernment returns to a context that names signs in the heavens and earth, says people pass them, and says they turn aside. The context root cue makes the non-dominant س م و to و س م mark-image available; the explicit sign and focus basira provide the independent contact that lets the image change the reading.
findings.reader_payoff: The heavens can appear not only as a place containing signs but, exploratorily, as a surface whose marks require a way of seeing.
findings.containment: The branch relies on a non-dominant cross-root mapping and is not a direct gloss of heavens. The ordinary reading of signs in the heavens and earth remains intact; this image is exploratory and does not claim that every celestial feature is a written mark.

epistemic.reason: The exact source coordinate and root match, and the context cue exposes the mapped branch, but the cross-root image is explicitly non-dominant and the HFT source is legacy_unbound.

branch_activations.carrier: The supplied trace maps the heavens occurrence to an available mark image while preserving its reported root س م و.

branch_activations.activation: The context cue's cross-root branch meets the explicit sign and passing relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The elevated field can be pictured as sign-bearing surface.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss or facet is supplied; the cross-root image is not a direct word gloss.

branch_activations.carrier: The supplied trace assigns the explicit sign occurrence the role of warrant for treating the scene as marked.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The heavens are named as the field people pass while turning aside.
branch_activations.activation: The sign and elevated field meet in the stated passage, while the focus supplies discernment as the return.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The marked-surface image becomes available beside the ordinary signs reading.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent branch gloss is supplied; the image remains exploratory.

branch_activations.activation: Basira returns to the sign-bearing field as a way to read what otherwise goes unnoticed.

branch_activations.boundary: This contextual image does not replace the focus's ordinary inner-understanding branch.

findings.title: The declared path answers a plea for guidance
findings.claim: In the added Fatiha verses, the focus's path of calling to Allah can be heard as an offered response to a communal plea for guidance, worship, and help, with the requested path bounded by the contrast named in 1:7.
findings.mechanism: The focus names its path, calls to Allah, and includes followers; 1:5 directs worship and reliance to Allah, 1:6 asks for guidance along the straight path, and 1:7 gives that path a specific human and moral contour. These individual ayat change the focus's path from a declaration alone into a possible answer to a shared request, while the focus's rejection of association keeps its destination undivided.
findings.reader_payoff: The path appears as something sought together and then offered for following, with worship and reliance as its orientation.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay from only 1:5-1:7, not a claim that the two path expressions are lexically identical or that the focus exhausts the Fatiha. The native pericope reading stands without it.

epistemic.reason: The channel evidence nominates the path and following relation; the three added ayat provide exact, distinct prayer, guidance, and path-boundary triggers, but their relation to the focus remains an overlay.

branch_activations.activation: The two path formulations meet in an explicit request for guidance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's route can be heard as answering a path that is already being sought.
